tools.name: actions_agent_get
tools.title: Get the actions assigned to an agent
tools.description:
The actions assigned to an agent: {agent_id, actions, active}. `actions` is every assigned name; `active` is the subset that has
an approved version — only those are tools of the agent (named action_<name>). Read-only. Scope actions:read.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

annotations.title: Get the actions assigned to an agent

tools.name: actions_agent_set
tools.title: Replace the actions assigned to an agent
tools.description:
Replace the whole list of actions assigned to an agent; returns {agent_id, actions, active}. Each assigned action with an
approved version becomes a tool of that agent (action_<name>), so this gives the agent new abilities on outside systems — ask the
user first. Read the current list with actions_agent_get and send every name the agent should keep: a name you leave out is
removed. A name with no approved version yet is stored but is not a tool until a person approves it; a name that does not exist
in the organization is refused (422 unknown_actions). The action's own risk level still applies to every call the agent makes.
The same list can be kept in a squad document (squad_export / squad_plan / squad_apply: an agent's "actions" key). Assignments are
not part of an agent's version history — to undo a change, set the previous list again. Scope actions:manage.

actions.description: Action names (at most 40). [] removes every action from the agent.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

annotations.title: Replace the actions assigned to an agent

tools.name: actions_connection_create
tools.title: Create an action connection
tools.description:
Create a connection: one outside system that actions may reach. Creating it sends nothing. Scope actions:manage.

The config never contains a secret value and this tool takes none. Store the secret as an Org Key in the web app (MCP & Keys)
and reference it by name: {cred:NAME} inside a header value, secret_name for a webhook. A header that looks like a credential
without a {cred:NAME} reference, or a name that is not an Org Key, is refused (422). Kind "simulate" sends nothing and returns
each action's fixed output — use it to try actions before a real system exists.

name.description: Lower-case letters, digits and underscores, 2–64 characters, starting with a letter (e.g. "erp"). Unique in the organization.

config.description:
Shape per kind. Omit for simulate.
http: {"base_url": "https://api.example.com/v1", "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer {cred:ERP_TOKEN}"},
"allowed_hosts": ["files.example.com"]} — https only; actions may call the base_url host and the listed hosts, nothing else.
An API that wants OAuth2 client credentials adds "auth": {"type": "oauth2_client_credentials", "token_url": "https://…",
"client_id": "<value or {cred:NAME}>", "client_secret": "{cred:NAME}", "scope"?: "…", "hosts": [<every allowed host that is
not the token server's host>]} and leaves the Authorization header out — Junis fetches the token and sends it as a Bearer token.
webhook: {"url": "https://hooks.example.com/junis", "secret_name": "ERP_WEBHOOK_SECRET"} — each event is signed
(Standard Webhooks v1) with the Org Key named by secret_name. That key must already exist. While the receiver switches to a
new secret, add "previous_secret_name": "<old Org Key>" and each event carries both signatures; remove it afterwards. If the user has no signing
secret yet, send them to the web app (Team → Actions → Connections → Add a connection → Webhook → "Create a new secret"):
Junis creates it there and shows it to them once, so the secret never passes through this conversation.
mcp: {"platform_id": "<id from list_mcp_platforms>"} — a remote MCP server registered in this organization.
simulate: {}

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

tools.name: actions_connection_delete
tools.title: Delete an action connection
tools.description:
Delete a connection. Confirm with the user first. Refused with 409 connection_in_use while approved actions use it (a person
disables those in the web app first). Scope actions:manage.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

tools.name: actions_connection_test
tools.title: Test an action connection (a webhook receives one signed ping)
tools.description:
Check a connection: {ok, message, …}. What it does depends on the kind, and for a webhook it is not a dry run:
http — checks the address and that the referenced Org Keys exist; sends nothing.
webhook — sends one signed `junis.ping` event to the endpoint (the receiving system sees it).
mcp — connects to the MCP server and returns its tools (name, description, input_schema) for writing an executor.
simulate — always ok; sends nothing.
Scope actions:manage.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

annotations.title: Test an action connection (a webhook receives one signed ping)

tools.name: actions_connection_update
tools.title: Change an action connection or turn it off/on
tools.description:
Change a connection's config or turn it off/on. Name and kind cannot be changed. Ask the user first. Scope actions:manage.

`config` replaces the whole config (same shape and rules as actions_connection_create — no secret values, {cred:NAME} references
only), so read the current one with actions_connections and send it complete. A connection that no approved action uses can be
changed freely. Turning a connection off (is_active=false) always works and stops every action that uses it. When approved
actions use the connection, changing its config or turning it back on (is_active=true) is refused with 409 connection_in_use:
that changes where approved actions send data, so a person does it in the web app (Team → Actions).

config.description: The complete new config. Omit to leave it unchanged.

is_active.description: false = off, true = on. Omit to leave it unchanged.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

annotations.title: Change an action connection or turn it off/on

tools.name: actions_connections
tools.title: List action connections
tools.description:
List the organization's action connections — the outside systems actions can reach: {items: [{id, name, kind, config,
is_active, …}]}. `config` holds addresses and Org Key names only, never secret values. Read-only. Scope actions:read.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

tools.name: actions_draft_create
tools.title: Create an action draft (a person approves it in the web app)
tools.description:
Create an action draft. A draft does nothing: no agent gets it and actions_run refuses it until a person approves it in the
web app (Team → Actions). This tool cannot approve. An approved version is never edited — creating a draft with the name of an
existing action makes its next version, which replaces the approved one only when a person approves it. If that name already has
an open draft the call answers 409 draft_exists with its definition_id: change it with actions_draft_update or delete it.
Check the draft with actions_dry_run before telling the user it is ready for approval. Scope actions:manage.

The definition fixes the address, headers and body shape; a caller or model supplies parameter values only. In executor strings,
"{param}" is replaced by that parameter's (or fixed_args') value; a string that is exactly "{param}" keeps the value's type
(number, boolean, object). A name that is neither a parameter nor a fixed arg is refused (422 invalid_action lists every error).

name.description: Lower-case letters, digits and underscores, 2–48 characters, starting with a letter. Agents see the tool action_<name>.

description.description: 10–2,000 characters. What the action does and when to use it — an agent decides from this text.

effect.description: "read", "write" or "destructive" — what it does to the outside system.

executor.description:
What is sent. Shape by the connection's kind:
http: {"method": "POST", "path": "/orders", "query": {...}, "headers": {...}, "body": {"part": "{part_no}", "qty": "{quantity}"}}
— method GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE; path starts with "/" and has no query string (use query); no body with GET/DELETE.
webhook: {"event_type": "order.created", "body": {...}} — delivered as {type, timestamp, data}.
mcp: {"tool": "<tool name from actions_connection_test>", "arguments": {...}} — omit arguments to pass the parameters as they are.
simulate, or no connection: {"output": {...}} — returned as the result; nothing is sent.

connection.description:
Name of the connection (actions_connections). Empty = a simulation with no connection. Without a connection, or
on a simulate connection, the executor may hold only "output": any other key is refused (422 invalid_action).

target_type.description: Knowledge map kind the action acts on, e.g. "Equipment" (optional).

params_schema.description:
JSON Schema object with top-level "properties" only (≤30) and "required". Types: string, integer, number,
boolean, array, object. A string parameter may carry "x-entity-type": "<Knowledge map kind>" — the value must then name an
entity of that kind (the platform resolves it; unknown or ambiguous names are refused) — and one such parameter may carry
"x-target": true to mark the run's target.

fixed_args.description: Values no caller can change, usable in the executor as "{name}". Names must differ from the parameters.

idempotent.description:
true only if repeating the request is harmless: the platform then retries timeouts and 5xx (up to 3 attempts).
false (default): a timeout is recorded as `unknown` and never retried.

risk.description:
"auto" (runs at once), "confirm" (one person confirms each run) or "two_person" (two different admins). Empty = the
default: auto for effect read, confirm otherwise. Do not lower it to avoid a confirmation unless the user asked for that.

preconditions.description:
Up to 10 conditions, all must hold: {"param": "quantity", "op": "lte", "value": 50} with op equals, not_equals,
in, lte, gte or exists; or {"roles": ["OWNER", "ADMIN", "MEMBER"]}. A roles rule checks the organization role of
whoever the run is for: the person who submits it in the web app, the owner of the session an agent is working in, or the
owner of the API key. With no roles rule, API keys must be owner/admin keys and an agent the action is assigned to can
run it for any user. Listing MEMBER also lets members' own API keys run it; a roles rule without MEMBER also stops
agents from running it on behalf of members.

summary_template.description: One line (≤300 characters) shown on approval cards and in the run log, e.g. "Order {quantity} × {part_no}".

timeout_s.description: 1–120 seconds for the request to the outside system (default 30).

rate_limit_per_hour.description: 1–10,000 runs per hour. Omit for no limit.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

annotations.title: Create an action draft (a person approves it in the web app)

tools.name: actions_draft_delete
tools.title: Delete an action draft
tools.description:
Delete a draft. Confirm with the user first. Only drafts: an approved or disabled version answers 409 not_a_draft, an id that
does not exist 404 not_found. Disabling an approved action is done by a person in the web app (Team → Actions); there is no tool for it.
Scope actions:manage.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

tools.name: actions_draft_update
tools.title: Replace an action draft
tools.description:
Replace a draft. Only a draft can be changed: an approved or disabled version answers 409 not_a_draft — create a new version
with actions_draft_create instead. The draft still does nothing until a person approves it in the web app (Team → Actions).
Scope actions:manage.

This is a full replacement, not a patch: read the draft with actions_get, then send every field it should keep. A field you
omit goes back to its default (no parameters, no preconditions, risk by effect, 30 s timeout …). The name cannot be changed, and
the connection is kept when `connection` is empty. Field meanings and executor shapes are the same as actions_draft_create.

definition_id.description: The draft's id (`id` of the draft version in actions_get, or definition_id from a 409 draft_exists).

description.description: 10–2,000 characters: what the action does and when to use it.

executor.description: What is sent, per the connection kind.

connection.description: Name of another connection to attach. Empty = keep the current one.

target_type.description: Knowledge map kind the action acts on.

idempotent.description: true only if repeating the request is harmless.

rate_limit_per_hour.description: Runs per hour. Omit for no limit.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

tools.name: actions_dry_run
tools.title: Preview the request an action would send (sends nothing)
tools.description:
Preview what one version of an action would send for the given arguments: {status: "dry_run", action, version, summary,
preview}. Sends nothing to the outside system, records no run, and shows secrets as ***. Works on drafts too — use it to check a
draft before asking a person to approve it. The arguments are validated exactly as in a real run (422 bad_arguments returns the
expected schema; 422 unknown_entity when an entity parameter does not resolve). When the arguments would not pass the action's
preconditions, the preview is still returned and carries would_fail: {code, message} — a real run would be refused for that
reason. Scope actions:manage.

definition_id.description: Id of the version to preview (from actions_get or the result of actions_draft_create).

args.description: Parameter values, as the action's params_schema describes them.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

annotations.title: Preview the request an action would send (sends nothing)

tools.name: actions_export
tools.title: Export actions as a junis.actions/v1 document
tools.description:
Export the organization's actions as one junis.actions/v1 document: {format, exported_at, connections: [{name, kind, config}],
actions: [{name, title, description, params_schema, executor, connection, effect, risk, …, exported_status}]}. Each action is the
version in use (the approved one, or the newest when none is approved). It holds no secret values — headers carry {cred:NAME} and a
webhook names its Org Key — and the MCP tool fingerprint is left out (it is pinned again when someone approves it). Read-only.
Scope actions:read (owner/admin key).

organization_id.description: UUID of the source organization. Always pass it.

annotations.title: Export actions as a junis.actions/v1 document

tools.name: actions_get
tools.title: Get one action with its versions
tools.description:
One action by name with every version: {name, latest, approved, versions}. `approved` is the version agents and actions_run
use right now (null when none is approved); `latest` may be a newer draft still waiting for a person. Each version carries its
`id` (the definition_id for actions_draft_update, actions_draft_delete and actions_dry_run). Read-only. Scope actions:read.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

annotations.title: Get one action with its versions

tools.name: actions_import
tools.title: Import a junis.actions/v1 document as drafts
tools.description:
Import a junis.actions/v1 document (from actions_export): {format, dry_run, connections: [{name, result, reason?, message?}],
actions: [{name, result, version?, reason?, message?}]}. result is would_create / created, exists (a connection with that name and
kind is kept as it is) or skipped (reason says why: kind_mismatch, draft_exists, missing_secret, connection_inactive, connection_not_found,
invalid_…). The preview runs the same checks as the import, so the Org Keys and MCP server a connection names must exist here.
Nothing is overwritten, every action comes in as a draft that a person approves in the web app, and one bad item does not stop the
rest. dry_run defaults to true: show the user that result first, then call again with dry_run=false only after they agree. The
Org Keys the document names must exist in the target organization. Scope actions:manage (owner/admin key).

document.description: The whole document object as actions_export returned it.

dry_run.description: true (default) writes nothing and reports what would happen; false imports.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

annotations.title: Import a junis.actions/v1 document as drafts

tools.name: actions_import_openapi
tools.title: Import OpenAPI operations as action drafts
tools.description:
Create an HTTP connection (or reuse one) and one action draft per chosen operation: {connection, created: [drafts]}.
All or nothing — if any chosen operation cannot be imported, 422 invalid_operations says why and nothing is saved. Everything
created is a draft: a person reviews name, description, effect and risk and approves each one in the web app (Team → Actions).
Only GET operations are imported as idempotent (safe for the platform to retry); for any other operation a person turns that on
during review. Run actions_import_openapi_preview first. Scope actions:manage.

spec.description: The same OpenAPI document text given to the preview (JSON or YAML, at most 2 MB).

connection.description:
{"name": "erp", "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer {cred:ERP_TOKEN}"}, "base_url": "https://…",
"allowed_hosts": [...]}. Only name is required. If an HTTP connection with that name exists it is reused as it is;
otherwise one is created with base_url (default: the document's server URL). Headers never hold a secret value — reference
an Org Key as {cred:NAME}.

operations.description: operation_id values from the preview (1–100) whose `importable` is true.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

annotations.title: Import OpenAPI operations as action drafts

tools.name: actions_import_openapi_preview
tools.title: Preview an OpenAPI import (writes nothing)
tools.description:
Read an OpenAPI document and list the operations that can become actions: {title, base_url, operations: [{operation_id,
method, path, summary, name, effect, risk, parameters, importable, errors, warnings}], warnings}. Writes nothing. Pick
operation_id values from here for actions_import_openapi. Scope actions:manage.

spec.description:
The OpenAPI document as text — JSON or YAML, OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 or Swagger 2.0, at most 2 MB. Pass the document itself,
not a URL (the platform does not fetch it).

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

tools.name: actions_list
tools.title: List action definitions (newest version per name)
tools.description:
List action definitions, one row per action name showing its newest version: {items: [{id, name, version, status, title,
description, params_schema, executor, effect, risk, tool_name, connection, …}]}. Filters apply to that newest version, so an
action whose newest version is a draft is listed as `draft` even when an older version is still approved and in use — use
actions_get for the full picture of one action. Read-only. Scope actions:read.

status.description:
"draft", "approved", "needs_check" or "disabled". Empty = all. needs_check = the MCP tool behind the action changed
after it was approved, so agents and runs stopped using it until a person approves it again in the web app or disables it.

target_type.description: Only actions whose target is this Knowledge map kind (exact match), e.g. "Equipment".

name.description: Only the action with exactly this name.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

annotations.title: List action definitions (newest version per name)

tools.name: actions_overview
tools.title: Actions overview (enabled, counts, pending approvals)
tools.description:
Whether Actions are on for the organization and how much exists: {enabled, connections, actions: {draft, approved, needs_check, disabled},
pending_approvals}. Start here. `enabled: false` (counts all zero) means Actions are switched off: every other actions_* tool then
answers 404 feature_disabled until a Junis administrator turns the feature on. Read-only. Scope actions:read (owner/admin key).

An action is a typed operation on an outside system (an HTTP API, a signed webhook, a tool of a registered MCP server, or a
simulation that sends nothing). Lifecycle: connection → draft → a person approves the draft in the web app (Team → Actions) →
assign it to an agent (actions_agent_set) or run it (actions_run).

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it: when omitted, the call acts in the key's default organization.

tools.name: actions_run
tools.title: Run an approved action on its target system
tools.description:
Run an approved action once and return {run_id, status, action, version, summary, http_status?, output?, error?,
approvals_needed?, expires_at?, idempotency_key}. This acts on an outside system — run it only when the user asked for that
effect. Scope actions:run. An owner's or admin's key can run every approved action. A member's key can run only an action
whose definition lists MEMBER in a roles precondition; any other answers 403 precondition_failed, and adding the scope to the
key does not change that — an admin allows members in the action's definition, or assigns the action to an agent instead.

An API key is not a person. An action with risk "auto" executes at once. An action with risk "confirm" or "two_person" is NOT
executed: the result is status "awaiting_approval" and a person approves or rejects it in the web app (Team → Actions) within
24 hours. This tool cannot approve, and no tool can.

Read `status` and report it to the user.
succeeded — done; `output` is the target system's answer (capped at 8,000 characters).
failed — the request never reached the target system, or the target answered with an error (`error`, `http_status`). After the
cause is fixed, a new request is fine.
unknown — the request was sent and then timed out or the connection dropped, or the run was interrupted (`error.code` may be
"interrupted"). The target system may have processed it. Never resend; the user checks the target system first.
awaiting_approval — not executed; waiting for a person. Follow it with actions_run_get(run_id).
executing — the approvals are complete and the platform is executing it now (a resend with the same key can show this). Do not
resend; read the outcome with actions_run_get(run_id).
rejected / expired — a person declined it, or nobody approved within 24 hours.
dry_run — the preview you asked for; nothing was sent.
Never call again to "retry" an awaiting_approval, executing or unknown result: awaiting_approval is already queued, executing is
under way, and an unknown run may have reached the target system. Tell the user instead.

Every call carries an idempotency key, so a resend cannot run the action twice: the same key with the same arguments returns the
first run (with replayed: true), even when the action is at its hourly limit; the same key with different arguments is refused
(idempotency_key_reused). When you do not pass
one, a new key is generated for this call and returned in the result — it protects against network-level resends only. Pass your
own stable key (for example an order or ticket id) whenever the same request might be sent again later. If this tool fails
without an answer (timeout, 5xx), the error message contains the key: look for the run with actions_runs(action=name) or call
again with that same key and the same args; never start it under a new key.

name.description: Name of an approved action (actions_list with status "approved").

args.description:
Parameter values, as the action's params_schema describes them (see actions_get). Wrong or missing values answer
422 bad_arguments with the expected schema. A value can never pick a secret: any value that contains an Org Key
reference ({cred:NAME}) is refused with bad_arguments, wherever it would go (header, body or query).

idempotency_key.description: Your own stable key for this request (at most 160 characters). Empty = one is generated for this call.

dry_run.description: true = validate and return the request that would be sent, without sending it or recording a run.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

annotations.title: Run an approved action on its target system

tools.name: actions_run_get
tools.title: Get one action run
tools.description:
One run: status, summary, who asked, approvals so far and how many are still needed, the target system's status code and
output preview, or the error. Use it to follow a run that came back `awaiting_approval`. Read-only. Scope actions:read.

run_id.description: The run_id from actions_run or actions_runs.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

tools.name: actions_runs
tools.title: List action runs
tools.description:
The run log, newest first: {items: [{run_id, status, action, version, summary, actor_kind, agent_name, args_preview,
http_status, output, error, approvals_needed, expires_at, created_at, …}]}. Every run is recorded, including failed, rejected and
expired ones. Use it to find a run you are unsure about before running anything again. Read-only. Scope actions:read.

state.description:
One of awaiting_approval (waiting for a person), executing (approvals complete, running now), succeeded, failed,
unknown (sent, then no answer or interrupted — the target may have processed it), rejected, expired. Empty = all.

action.description: Only runs of this action name.

target_entity_id.description: Only runs whose target is this Knowledge entity id.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

tools.title: Add sub-agent
tools.description: Add a sub-agent to a parent agent.

child_agent_id.description: UUID of the agent to add as sub-agent.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it: when omitted, the call acts in the key's default organization.

tools.name: apply_team_changes
tools.title: Apply batch team changes
tools.description:
Apply batch team structure changes. Not transactional — each action is independent.

The batch is checked first (known action, required keys). If any change would be rejected, nothing
is sent: the result has "applied": false and "rejected": [{index, action, reason}] (also mirrored in
"errors") — fix those items and send the batch again. Once sent, a change that fails on the platform
lands in "errors" while the others still apply; retry only those.

True = only check the batch and report {"dry_run", "valid", "rejected", "count"};
nothing is sent.

tools.name: assign_skill
tools.title: Assign skill to agent
tools.description: Assign a skill to an agent.

skill_id.description: UUID of the skill to assign.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it: when omitted, the call acts in the key's default organization.

tools.name: cancel_run
tools.title: Stop a running session
tools.description:
Stop the run in progress on a session (the same signal as the web Stop button).

A streaming run stops within about a second and its in-flight model call is billed up to the stop. A non-streaming
run (start_run, send_message, the kit run command) stops between steps: the model call or tool call in progress
finishes and is billed, then the run saves what it has with "[Response interrupted]" and returns it. An idle
session answers 409 not_processing; a run started before the server supported this answers 409 not_cancellable.

session_id.description: The session whose run should stop.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

on_behalf_of.description: The provisioned account the run belongs to, if any.

tools.name: chat_completion
tools.title: Chat with organization orchestrator
tools.description:
OpenAI-compatible chat completion request (waits up to 10 minutes).

Same long-run rule as send_message: if it times out the run continues server-side — do not
resend and do not send another message into that session; poll get_run(session_id) until it
finishes. Pass a new UUID as session_id (or use start_run) so a timed-out run can be followed;
without one, find it with list_sessions (pick the one with your own user_id).

model.description: Echoed back only (the orchestrator's configured model is always used).

agent_id.description:
IGNORED — this endpoint always talks to the organization orchestrator. To message a
specific agent use send_message(agent_id, ...). Kept for backward compatibility.

session_id.description:
Session UUID. An existing one of yours continues that conversation; a new UUID
creates the session with that id.

temperature.description:
Accepted for OpenAI compatibility but NOT applied — the backend handler never
reads it; the agent's configured temperature is used. Change it with update_agent instead.

max_tokens.description: Same — accepted but not applied; the agent's configured max_output_tokens is used.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it: when omitted, the call acts in the key's default organization.

tools.name: clone_agent
tools.title: Clone agent
tools.description:
Clone an agent within the same organization (most settings; include_contents, max_llm_calls and some other fields are not copied — check the clone with get_agent).

MCP links are copied without their per-agent tool selection, so the clone gets every tool of each
platform (larger prompts, higher cost). Sub-agents, skills, Composio and device links are not copied.

agent_id.description: UUID of the agent to clone.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it: when omitted, the call acts in the key's default organization.

tools.name: create_agent
tools.title: Create agent
tools.description: Create a new agent. LLM_AGENT requires name+model+instruction.

name.description: Letters, digits and underscores, unique within the organization (spaces and hyphens become underscores at run time; a name that collides after that is rejected).

model.description:
LLM model identifier from list_llm_models (LLM_AGENT only). When the request names no model,
prefer the newest direct OpenAI GPT model for the role (e.g. openai/gpt-6.1-sol general,

tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific MCP platform.

Credential values come back masked ('••••••'): every value in decrypted_auth_config; in decrypted_config,
values under a credential name (X-Key, DB_PASS, api_keys, lists included; a variable description's type,
description, label and required stay visible), the value of an entry named like a credential
({"name": "Authorization", "value": ...}), --api-key VALUE / --token=... / API_KEY=... / "Authorization: ..."
anywhere in an argument or the command, token-shaped values (sk-, xoxb-, ghp_, JWT, Slack/Discord webhook
addresses) and any argument that embeds a URL credential (or is longer than 8 KB). After a flag, an =
assignment or a one-word name:value, a value stays readable when it is a mode word (none, oauth2, true), a
complete template (${TOKEN}, {{...}}), a file path or a number or word of up to 8 letters; in a hyphenated
header line, a {name, value} entry or under a credential-named key only a template or a value made of mode words
alone (X-Api-Key: Bearer abc... is masked; a lone {"key": ...} without a value field holds a value and is masked);
after a password-like name only none-like words and templates; after Authorization/Cookie only templates
(POSTGRES_PASSWORD=password, --password admin, X-Api-Key: abcdefgh and Authorization: Bearer password are
masked). Text under description/note keys is checked for token shapes and addresses only; an entry's own
name/key field stays readable. Ordinary values such as --max-tokens 4096,
--use-jwt true or --auth oauth2 stay readable. Key names stay, so you can see which credentials are configured
without copying secrets into the conversation. Sending a masked value back in update_mcp_platform keeps the
stored value. A server address with a credential in it is masked as a whole and mcp_server_url_host names its
host: a user:password@ or token@ part, or a query/fragment parameter whose name ends in key, token, secret,
auth, password, pass, pw, code, config, signature, credential, jwt, pat or bearer, plurals and encoded names
included (api_key, apiKey, access_token, api%5Fkey; count and page names like max_tokens and page_token are
not masked). A secret with no name and no known shape is not detected. create_mcp_platform refuses a masked
address. A global (shared) platform is always returned masked (credentials, every setting except variable
descriptions and the command, and the address); organization_is_active shows whether this organization
switched it on.

tools.name: start_run
tools.title: Start agent run (returns at once)
tools.description:
Start an agent run and return its session_id without waiting for the answer. Poll with get_run.

Use this instead of send_message / chat_completion for anything that may take minutes (team builds,
research, multi-agent workflows). The run executes and bills exactly like send_message. Never call
start_run again for the same work — poll get_run(session_id); a second call is a second run.

Returns {"session_id", "status", "poll_with": "get_run"} where status is:
  "running"   — the platform shows the run in progress;
  "completed" — it finished within the first seconds; "result" holds the answer;
  "failed"    — it finished with an error; "result" holds the error text;
  "starting"  — the request is in flight but the run was not visible yet; poll get_run.
A request the platform rejects outright (credits, permissions, unknown agent) raises an error and
nothing runs.

agent_id.description: UUID of the agent to run. Empty = the organization orchestrator.

session_id.description: Continue this session. Use a new id or one of your OWN sessions: an id owned by another real person makes the platform run in a derived session that get_run cannot find, and a session of a provisioned account is taken over (it moves to you unless on_behalf_of is passed). Empty = a new session id is generated.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it: when omitted, the call acts in the key's default organization.

on_behalf_of.description:
Run as a provisioned account of your organization (requires the users:delegate
scope). Pass the same value to get_run.

max_llm_calls.description:
Optional budget — stop this run after this many model calls. Can only lower the agent's
saved limit; 0 = the saved limit.

tools.name: update_mcp_platform
tools.title: Update MCP platform
tools.description:
Update an MCP platform. Only provided fields are changed.
Same parameters as create_mcp_platform, plus platform_id. Local config fields (command / args /
env_vars_schema / cli_args_mapping) are merged into the stored config, so sending only `args`
keeps the existing command and env schema. The credentials are one stored object: env_vars or
auth_config REPLACES it as a whole (keys you leave out are removed; a masked '••••••' value sent
back keeps the stored one; inside a list such as args, masked values are restored in the order they were
masked: plain items around them may be added, removed or changed (adding and removing in the same update is
checked strictly), a masked value may be removed when the update only removes items, and several entries of a
list of objects may be edited in place at once, each keeping its own values; masked values that moved (even
one), a run of adjacent masked values only partly replaced, an entry changed and moved at once, one of two
same-shaped entries gone while something else took its place, or tens of thousands of items are refused with
400 masked_placeholder rather than guessed — make one kind of change at a time). auth_type alone keeps the
stored credentials and changes only that label. A global (shared) platform cannot be changed this way
(403 global_platform): use toggle_mcp_active to switch it on or off for this organization.

platform_id.description: UUID of the MCP platform to update.

tools.name: knowledge_changes
tools.title: graph changes since a cursor
tools.description:
What changed in the knowledge graph since a cursor (or a time): entities (`created` · `updated` · `merged`, with attrs) and relations (`added` · `invalidated`),
oldest first, each up to `limit`. No model call. For a dashboard: draw once from `knowledge_graph_snapshot`, then poll this with the returned `cursor`
(keep calling right away while `has_more` is true). The External API also has an SSE form, `GET /api/external/brain/changes/stream`, for a server that
keeps a connection open. Deletions are not in the feed (a removed source, a `replace` re-import) — redraw from the snapshot now and then; the cursor
never skips a slow import (it stops at the oldest write still in progress, `watermark`). Organization admin or owner key. Read-only.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

cursor.description: The `cursor` of the previous reply (opaque). When given, `since` is ignored.

since.description: "YYYY-MM-DD" (start of that day, UTC) or ISO datetime — where to start when there is no cursor yet. Empty with no cursor = everything.

limit.description: 1–500 per list (default 200). types: Comma-separated entity kinds to include (relations are not filtered).

tools.name: knowledge_entities_update_attrs
tools.title: Update entity attributes (state) without re-import
tools.description:
Update attributes (state) of existing entities by `type` + `external_id` without re-importing: merges `attrs` into each entity — no document, card or
embedding is created, so it costs no credits and takes up to 500 entities per call. For values that change often (a position, a stock level, a status).
Same attribute rules as import: only attributes declared for that kind are kept (others are dropped and counted), values are stored as strings (≤200 chars),
the newest value wins, `external_id` itself cannot be changed. Unknown kinds or entities not yet imported → 422 and nothing is written
(`on_missing="skip"` skips the missing ones). Updated entities show up in `knowledge_changes` as `updated`. Admin key, scope brain:manage.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

on_missing.description: "error" (default — any missing entity rejects the whole call) or "skip".

`custom`, and `graph_limits`. Read this before `knowledge_map_apply_preset` / `knowledge_map_extend` when a domain map is bigger than the defaults.
Admin key. Read-only.

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

tools.name: knowledge_map_set_limits
tools.title: Raise the knowledge map caps (confirm_cost)
tools.description:
Raise the organization's knowledge-map caps (kinds · relations · properties per kind) so a larger domain map fits — the same rules as the web app:
never below the defaults (12/24/12 → 422 `limits_below_default`), never below the current map (422 `limits_below_map`), hard caps 48/96/24, and raising
above the defaults needs `confirm_cost=true` (otherwise 422 `limits_confirm_required` with the cost estimate — extraction input grows with the number of
kinds and the source budget runs out sooner). Audited. Admin key, scope brain:manage.

types.description: Kinds cap (12–48). predicates: Relations cap (24–96). properties: Properties-per-kind cap (12–24).

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it.

confirm_cost.description: Pass true after showing the user the estimate from the 422 reply. exclude_default: Do not count the default kinds toward the cap.

`knowledge_geo_near`. No model call.

attr.description: Location attribute name (default "location"). type: Kind filter. limit: 1–500. include_attrs: Also return each entity's attributes.

The organization's knowledge-change webhook (`config`: url, secret_name, types, enabled — no secret value) and its delivery status (`status`: cursor,
last_sent_at, last_status, last_error, failures, sent_total). `config` is null when none is registered. Admin key. Read-only.

tools.name: knowledge_changes_webhook_set
tools.title: Register or change the knowledge-change webhook
tools.description:
Register or change the knowledge-change webhook: every minute the platform POSTs what changed since the last delivery (same body as `knowledge_changes`,
Standard Webhooks headers `webhook-id` / `webhook-timestamp` / `webhook-signature`) to `url`. The first tick only sets the baseline; a non-2xx keeps the
cursor and retries next minute — the same page carries the same `webhook-id` (dedupe on it), a page that grew in the meantime gets a new one; 120 consecutive
failures turn it off, and saving again (this tool) resets that counter while keeping the cursor. `secret_name` is the name of an organization secret (Org Key)
that holds the signing secret — pass the name, never the value. Admin key, scope brain:manage.

url.description: https address of the receiver. secret_name: Org Key name holding the signing secret (Standard Webhooks `whsec_…` recommended).

organization_id.description: UUID of the target organization. Always pass it. types: Optional entity kinds to include. enabled: false parks it without removing.

annotations.title: Register or change the knowledge-change webhook
